title: Laptop Battery Not Charging
cardText: Diagnose a laptop battery that does not charge, charges slowly or stops at a fixed percentage.
Check charging limits, charger recognition, power delivery, battery health and Windows settings.
Identify charger, battery, firmware and internal charging circuit faults.
text: This guide is for Windows laptops that operate but have battery charging problems.
Start by identifying whether the charge percentage is increasing or has stopped.
Check manufacturer battery protection settings and charger compatibility before replacing hardware.
Use Windows battery reports and manufacturer diagnostics to assess battery condition.
If the laptop does not power on at all, use the Computer Won't Turn On guide.

checkBatteryPercentage.title: Check actual charging behaviour
body: With the charger connected, note the current battery percentage.
Observe whether the percentage increases over approximately 15 to 30 minutes.
Check whether Windows reports charging, plugged in but not charging, or no external power.
If the percentage increases but charging is unusually slow, investigate charger wattage and laptop power consumption.
If charging stops consistently at a particular percentage, check manufacturer charging limits.

chargingWorking.title: Battery charging normally
body: The battery percentage is increasing at an expected rate.
Charging appears to be functioning correctly.
If charging is much slower than expected, check the charger's rated wattage and whether the laptop is under heavy load.
A battery near full capacity may charge more slowly by design.

batteryManagementCheck.title: Check manufacturer battery charging limits
body: Some laptops deliberately stop charging at a configured percentage to reduce battery wear.
Check the manufacturer's battery management application or BIOS settings.
Examples include Lenovo Vantage Conservation Mode, Dell Battery Charge Configuration and ASUS Battery Health Charging.
Depending on the manufacturer and model, charging may stop at approximately 60%, 80% or another configured threshold.
Charging may also pause when the battery is already close to full.
If the battery consistently stops at a particular percentage, determine whether a charging threshold is enabled.

batteryManagementCheck.caption: Battery conservation settings may intentionally prevent charging beyond a configured percentage.

disableBatteryLimit.title: Adjust the battery charging limit
body: Open the manufacturer's battery management application or supported BIOS charging settings.
Review the current charging limit and confirm whether it explains the observed behaviour.
If a full charge is required, temporarily disable or increase the configured charging threshold.
Save the setting and reconnect the charger if necessary.
Check whether the battery begins charging beyond the previous limit.
For laptops normally used on mains power, retaining a conservation limit may be preferable for battery lifespan.

link.name: Lenovo: Conservation Mode settings
link.description: Explains why charging may stop at a fixed percentage and how to change the setting.

checkWindowsBatteryStatus.title: Check whether Windows recognises external power
body: Open Windows battery and power settings.
Check whether the laptop reports that external power is connected.
Look for messages such as Plugged in, Not charging or a warning about a weak charger.
A laptop can recognise external power without receiving enough power to charge the battery.
If the charger is not recognised, investigate the adapter and power connection.
If external power is recognised, check whether the charger provides sufficient wattage.

link.name: Dell: AC adapter recognition and charging
link.description: Explains how adapter detection problems can prevent battery charging.

inspectCharger.title: Inspect charger and charging port
body: Inspect the charger cable, connector and power adapter for visible damage.
Check for frayed cables, bent pins, damaged insulation or signs of overheating.
Inspect the laptop charging port for looseness, damage or obvious debris.
For USB-C charging, check that the cable and port support charging at the required power level.
If the laptop supports multiple charging ports, test another supported port where appropriate.
Do not use a damaged charger or attempt to straighten damaged charging contacts.

link.name: Dell: Identify AC adapter damage
link.description: Manufacturer guidance for inspecting chargers, charging ports and adapter recognition faults.

replaceCharger.title: Replace damaged charger
body: The charger or its cable appears damaged.
Stop using the affected component.
Replace it with a manufacturer-approved or properly compatible charger.
Confirm the output voltage, power rating and connector are suitable for the laptop.
For USB-C charging, use a charger and cable that support the required USB Power Delivery wattage.
If the laptop charging port itself is damaged, arrange repair rather than repeatedly connecting chargers.

checkPowerOutlet.title: Check external power delivery
body: Test the wall outlet with another known-working device.
Bypass power boards, extension leads and surge protectors during testing.
Connect the charger directly to a known-working outlet.
If the outlet is working and the charger is still not recognised, test another compatible adapter.

restorePower.title: External power fault identified
body: The outlet or power board is not supplying reliable power.
Use a known-working outlet and replace faulty extension leads or power boards.
Do not use damaged outlets or equipment showing signs of overheating.
Retest battery charging once reliable external power is available.

testAlternateCharger.title: Test another compatible charger
body: Test with a known-working charger approved for the laptop or confirmed compatible with its specifications.
Match the correct voltage, connector and required wattage.
For USB-C devices, ensure the replacement supports the appropriate USB Power Delivery profile.
Check whether Windows recognises the replacement and the battery begins charging.
If the replacement works, the original charger or its cable is likely responsible.
If neither charger works, continue investigating adapter recognition and battery charging.

link.name: Dell: AC adapter troubleshooting
link.description: Official methods for identifying charging failures caused by incompatible or faulty adapters.

chargerFaultFound.title: Original charger fault likely
body: The battery charges correctly with another compatible charger.
The original charger, cable or adapter identification circuitry is likely faulty.
Replace the original charger with a compatible unit of sufficient power capacity.
Confirm the battery charges normally after replacement.

checkChargerRating.title: Check charger wattage and recognition
body: Compare the charger's rated output power with the laptop manufacturer's requirements.
A low-wattage adapter may power a laptop but charge the battery slowly or not at all under load.
For USB-C charging, confirm that the charger, cable and port support the required USB Power Delivery level.
Some manufacturers display the detected AC adapter type or wattage in BIOS or their diagnostic application.
On supported Dell laptops, an Unknown adapter type can indicate charger, connector or identification problems.
If the charger is correctly recognised and provides sufficient power, continue with battery troubleshooting.

link.name: Dell: Troubleshoot battery charging
link.description: Explains AC adapter wattage, recognition and charging failures.

chargerUnderpowered.title: Charger compatibility or recognition problem
body: The connected charger may not provide the required wattage or may not be recognised correctly.
Check the laptop manufacturer's adapter specifications.
Use a known-working compatible charger with sufficient power.
For USB-C devices, verify the charging port and cable also support the required power.
If a correctly rated adapter still appears as Unknown, investigate the charging port and internal adapter identification circuitry.
Avoid replacing the battery until the charger has been properly verified.

link.name: Dell: Identify adapter recognition faults
link.description: Manufacturer guidance for chargers reported as Unknown or incorrectly rated.

powerReset.title: Perform a laptop power reset
body: Shut down Windows and disconnect the charger and unnecessary USB devices.
For laptops with an externally removable battery, remove it according to the manufacturer's instructions.
If the manufacturer recommends a standard residual-power reset, hold the power button for approximately 15 to 30 seconds.
Reconnect the battery if removed, then reconnect the charger.
Restart the laptop and check whether battery charging resumes.
Some models require a specific embedded controller reset procedure or reset button.
Do not dismantle a sealed laptop merely to disconnect its internal battery.

link.name: HP: Laptop battery and adapter troubleshooting
link.description: Official battery troubleshooting, including hard resets and battery diagnostics.

checkBatteryHealth.title: Check Windows battery health report
body: Open Command Prompt or Windows Terminal.
Run the command: powercfg /batteryreport
Windows will generate an HTML battery report and display the saved file location.
Open the report and find the Installed batteries section.
Compare Design Capacity with Full Charge Capacity.
A significantly reduced Full Charge Capacity indicates battery wear.
Review the battery's recent usage and capacity history if available.
Capacity loss alone does not prove that a charging failure is caused by the battery.

link.name: Microsoft: Battery care and battery reports
link.description: Official instructions for generating a Windows battery report and understanding battery deterioration.

checkBatteryHealth.alt: Windows battery report highlighting Design Capacity and Full Charge Capacity
checkBatteryHealth.caption: Compare the current full charge capacity with the original design capacity to assess battery wear.

checkBatteryDiagnostics.title: Run manufacturer battery diagnostics
body: Run the battery diagnostic utility provided by the laptop manufacturer.
Examples include Dell preboot diagnostics, HP Battery Check and Lenovo hardware diagnostics.
Review whether the battery is detected correctly and whether the test reports a fault.
Record any battery health status, error message or diagnostic failure code.
A battery may have reasonable remaining capacity but still fail due to internal electronics or charging faults.
Replace the battery only when diagnostics and other evidence identify it as defective.
If the battery passes, continue with software and firmware checks.

link.name: HP: Battery Check
link.description: Official HP diagnostic tool for battery condition and failure identification.

link.name: Dell: Laptop battery diagnostics
link.description: Official guidance for checking battery health and running hardware tests.

replaceBattery.title: Battery replacement required
body: Manufacturer diagnostics indicate that the battery is defective or has reached the end of its useful life.
Confirm the correct replacement part for the laptop model.
Use a compatible, reputable battery replacement.
For laptops with sealed internal batteries, follow manufacturer service procedures or arrange professional replacement.
Do not attempt to charge, puncture or reuse a swollen or damaged battery.
Confirm charging and battery operation after replacement.

link.name: Microsoft: Battery safety
link.description: Guidance on battery deterioration, swelling and safe handling.

checkBatteryDriver.title: Check Windows battery drivers
body: Open Device Manager and expand Batteries.
Look for Microsoft AC Adapter and Microsoft ACPI-Compliant Control Method Battery, where supported.
Check for warning symbols or device error codes.
If the battery device has a Windows driver problem, uninstall only the affected battery device and restart Windows to allow it to be detected again.
Do not uninstall unrelated chipset or power management drivers.
Check the laptop manufacturer's website for relevant chipset or power management driver updates.
Retest battery charging after restarting.

checkFirmware.title: Check BIOS and charging firmware
body: Check the laptop manufacturer's support page for BIOS, embedded controller and power management updates relevant to battery charging.
Review the update release notes for fixes related to batteries or AC adapter detection.
Check the existing BIOS charging settings for unexpected restrictions.
Do not install firmware updates while the laptop has unreliable power unless the manufacturer's recovery or update procedure specifically supports it.
If no relevant update is available, continue with hardware diagnostics.

link.name: Dell: Battery and BIOS charging settings
link.description: Official information about firmware, adapter detection and battery charging configuration.

updateFirmware.title: Apply relevant firmware update
body: Confirm that the update is intended for the exact laptop model.
Read the manufacturer's update instructions and power requirements.
Ensure the system has a stable power source and meets the required battery charge level.
Check whether BitLocker protection must be suspended and confirm the recovery key is available before making firmware changes.
Do not interrupt a firmware update once started.
Restart the laptop and retest charging after the update.
If reliable power cannot be guaranteed, do not attempt the update.

hardwareFault.title: Further charging hardware diagnostics required
body: Battery charging still fails after checking charger recognition, power delivery, battery health, Windows drivers and relevant firmware.
Possible causes include a damaged charging port, faulty internal charging circuitry, battery communication faults or motherboard problems.
Test with a confirmed compatible charger before replacing internal components.
Review manufacturer diagnostic results and any BIOS adapter recognition warnings.
If the battery is swollen, the laptop becomes unusually hot or the charging port is damaged, stop using the affected hardware.
Record the laptop model, charger rating, battery diagnostic results and troubleshooting history.
Arrange further hardware diagnosis or repair.
